methodological_rigor.justification: The retrospective single-center design with only 29 patients is severely underpowered for the primary workflow-survival associations; no a priori power or sample-size calculation is reported. Confounding by indication for pre-biopsy corticosteroid exposure is acknowledged in the Discussion but not addressed analytically (no propensity score, no stratification by MSKCC class, no adjustment for baseline severity). The authors explicitly avoid multivariable Cox regression due to insufficient events-per-variable, which is honest but leaves every reported association unadjusted. Steroid exposure is dichotomized without dose/duration data, and the 7-day MRI-to-biopsy cut-off is described as reflecting workflow convention rather than biological validation. KM/log-rank are appropriate choices and endpoints are pre-specified, but no confidence intervals, hazard ratios, or effect sizes accompany the median survivals, and non-significant results (p=0.127, p=0.074, p=0.095) are repeatedly characterized as showing 'clear separation', which overreaches given the data.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a small (n=29) single-center retrospective cohort of consecutive PCNSL patients across a decade with no external comparator; this maps to Oxford LoE 4 (low-quality cohort/case series). PCNSL is a legitimately time-sensitive, understudied malignancy, and the framing of modifiable neurosurgical-phase variables (pre-biopsy steroid avoidance, expedited biopsy) is clinically actionable and resource-neutral, which supports moderate translational interest. However, the headline associations do not reach statistical significance, confounding by indication is explicitly acknowledged for the strongest signal (steroids), and endpoints like OS/PFS are patient-relevant but the generalizability from a 29-patient series is limited. The findings are explicitly framed as hypothesis-generating and could motivate quality-improvement audits or multicenter prospective designs but do not currently inform guidelines.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE is the applicable checklist for this retrospective observational cohort. Key STROBE items that are reasonably covered include study design/setting, eligibility criteria, variable definitions, outcome definitions (OS and PFS from biopsy), and statistical methods. Gaps include absence of a participant flow diagram, no reporting of how many patients were screened versus excluded at each step, no discussion of missing data handling, no confidence intervals for median survivals, no reporting of loss to follow-up, and no explicit statement about ethics approval, consent, or protocol registration in the retained text. The manuscript contains a visible '[REDACTED]' artifact in the Discussion that signals incomplete copy. No data availability, code sharing, or supplementary analytic code are mentioned beyond a referenced Supplementary Figure S1, warranting a floor data/code score.

novelty_literature.justification: The empirical focus — pre-biopsy corticosteroid exposure, MRI-to-biopsy interval, and biopsy-to-induction timing in PCNSL — is well-trodden ground; references 11, 16-19 cited by the authors themselves show these variables and their diagnostic/prognostic implications have been examined in larger series (e.g., Houillier et al. LOC network, Tringale et al. n=559). The reframing as 'neurosurgical workflow' and the emphasis on the pre-oncology entry window is a modest conceptual packaging novelty rather than a new mechanism, assay, or population. No new methodology is introduced, and because the central comparisons are not statistically significant in n=29, the empirical contribution is incremental confirmation of directional trends already reported. Positioning is competent and does not over-claim 'first', but the gap argument is weak given existing larger real-world cohorts on diagnostic delay and steroid exposure.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is readable with a logical IMRaD flow, and inclusion/exclusion criteria plus variable definitions are explicit. Weaknesses include a conspicuously duplicated abstract (two near-identical narrative blocks), a visible '[REDACTED]' token in Section 4 indicating incomplete redaction/editing, and lists in Methods rendered without proper line breaks (inclusion/exclusion criteria run together as single lines). Several sentences overstate the data (e.g., 'clear separation of survival curves' when p>0.05) and the Discussion contains minor stylistic awkwardness ('it is therefore paradoxical that neurosurgeons…'). Table/figure captions are referenced but numerical consistency between text and Table 2 for the >7-day MRI-to-biopsy group is reported as a range ('5 and 7 months') rather than a point estimate, which is unusual.

key_strengths: Clinically actionable framing of modifiable, resource-neutral pre-oncology workflow variables in a time-sensitive malignancy
Consecutive, decade-long single-center cohort treated under a standardized hematology protocol, limiting systemic-therapy heterogeneity
Pre-specified categorical cut-offs for MRI-to-biopsy interval and transparent, honest acknowledgment of exploratory/hypothesis-generating status
Internal validity support via expected MSKCC prognostic discrimination (p=0.038 for OS)
key_concerns: Severely underpowered sample (n=29) with no power calculation; primary workflow comparisons do not reach significance (p=0.127, 0.074, 0.095) yet are repeatedly described as showing 'clear separation'
Confounding by indication for pre-biopsy steroids acknowledged narratively but not addressed analytically (no propensity scoring, no stratification by MSKCC/severity, no multivariable modeling)

Reporting gaps against STROBE: no participant flow diagram, no confidence intervals on median survivals, no hazard ratios, no missing-data handling, no ethics statement in retained text, no data/code availability statement
Visible '[REDACTED]' artifact in Discussion and duplicated abstract indicate incomplete manuscript preparation
Novelty is incremental; larger real-world cohorts (LOC network, MSKCC Tringale) have already examined steroid exposure and diagnostic delay
Steroid exposure dichotomized without dose/duration; MRI-to-biopsy cut-offs chosen by workflow convention rather than biological validation
chief_reviewer.rationale: A transparently exploratory 29-patient single-center retrospective cohort with no statistically significant primary findings, incomplete reporting (STROBE gaps, visible redaction artifact, duplicated abstract), and only incremental novelty over existing larger PCNSL real-world series. The clinical framing is valuable but the evidence base is thin; appropriate venue is tier 4 and only with substantial revisions to tighten statistical interpretation, add STROBE elements, remove editorial artifacts, and reframe conclusions proportionate to the non-significant results.
